user.title: What should PowerPlan help you with?
user.description: Pick one; you can change it later. Most Norwegian homes want to save on both energy and the grid fee. [How this works]({docs})

menu_options.full: Save on energy and grid fee

name.title: What do you want to call this home?
name.description: The name goes on the home's device and its entities.

data_description.name: Home Assistant's own name for your home, unless you choose another.

timezone.title: Which timezone is the house in?
timezone.description: Home Assistant has no timezone set, so PowerPlan asks. Window boundaries, deadlines and when tomorrow's prices are due all depend on it. [How this works]({docs})

data_description.timezone: The IANA time zone the house is in.

electrical.title: How big is your main fuse?
electrical.description: The fuse sets how much the whole home can draw. If you are unsure, choose Don't know and PowerPlan assumes the usual size. [How this works]({docs})

data_description.country: Home Assistant has no country set, so it is asked here.
data_description.system: It says on the fuse box or your grid bill.
data_description.main_fuse_a: It is printed on the main fuse in the fuse box.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.description: Filled in from your country and fuse.

data_description.per_phase_limit_a: Only if your grid company set a lower limit per phase than the fuse.
data_description.phases: How many phases the home is connected with.
data_description.export_limit_kw: Advanced: the most your grid company lets you export, in kW; empty if none.

meter.title: Where do you measure your electricity use?
meter.description: Pick the device that reads your electricity meter, such as an AMS/HAN reader or a P1 dongle. Leave it empty to pick the sensors yourself. [How this works]({docs})

data_description.device: Only devices that measure power are listed.

meter_roles.title: Which sensor measures what?
meter_roles.description: Power now and the meter reading are the two that matter. Everything else is optional. [How this works]({docs})

data_description.grid_power: What the whole home draws from the grid right now.
data_description.import_register: The meter's total reading in kWh, bought from the grid.
data_description.export_register: The total kWh sold back, if you have solar panels.
data_description.production_power: What your solar panels produce right now.
data_description.meter_window: Some meters publish this hour's use themselves.

per_phase.name: Per phase
per_phase.description: Current on each phase, if your meter reports it.

data_description.phase_current_l1: Amps on phase 1; only useful with all three.

prices.title: What contract do you have with your electricity supplier?
prices.description: Your supplier sells you the energy; your grid company's tariff comes on top. PowerPlan needs tomorrow's prices to plan tonight. [How this works]({docs})

data_description.source: Spot price follows the market hour by hour; Norgespris is the state's fixed price.

prices_nordpool.title: Which price area are you in?
prices_nordpool.description: PowerPlan reads the prices through the Nord Pool integration. Tomorrow's prices usually arrive early in the afternoon. [How this works]({docs})

data_description.config_entry: Which Nord Pool entry to read prices through.
data_description.area: Where your home is; it is on your electricity bill.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.description: Already filled in. Open it only if you know you want something else.

data_description.publication_tz: Advanced: the market's publication time zone; leave empty to use the price area's.
data_description.publication_time: Advanced: when tomorrow's prices usually appear; leave empty to use the price area's.

prices_entity.title: Which sensor has your prices?
prices_entity.description: Pick the sensor that already carries a price curve. PowerPlan recognizes the common formats and tells you which one it detected. [How this works]({docs})

data_description.entity_id: The sensor whose attributes hold the hours and their prices.
data_description.format: Detected from the sensor's integration; change it only if the prices come out wrong.

prices_fixed.title: What do you pay per kWh?
prices_fixed.description: With no curve to follow, PowerPlan cannot move usage to a cheaper hour — but it still counts your cost and keeps you in your capacity step. [How this works]({docs})

data_description.price: In øre (or cents) per kWh, as on your bill.

modifiers.title: What does your supplier add, on top of the grid tariff?
modifiers.description: The grid tariff from {operator} already covers {covered}, and taxes come next. Tick only what your contract with the supplier adds. [How this works]({docs})

data_description.modifiers: Leave one out and it is simply not part of your price.

modifier_spot_scale.title: Does your supplier add a markup?
modifier_spot_scale.description: The markup is on your electricity bill or in your contract. [How this works]({docs})

data_description.mult: Your supplier's factor on the spot price; 1 means no change.
data_description.offset: Added to every kWh, in your currency.

modifier_fixed_price.title: What is your fixed price?
modifier_fixed_price.description: A state scheme such as Norgespris replaces the spot price up to a monthly cap. The price is in your agreement. [How this works]({docs})

data_description.price: In øre (or cents) per kWh, without VAT; VAT is added on top.
data_description.cap_kwh_per_month: How many kWh a month the fixed price covers; spot applies above it.

modifier_day_type.title: What do the special days cost?
modifier_day_type.description: Some tariffs price announced days, such as critical peak days, differently. The prices are in your agreement. [How this works]({docs})

data_description.rates: The announced day types and what each costs.
data_description.fallback: The day type used when nothing is announced.
data_description.entity: The sensor whose state is the day's type, such as tomorrow's Tempo color.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.description: Already filled in. Open it only if you know you want something else.

data_description.day_offset: Advanced: 1 when the sensor shows tomorrow's type today, 0 when it shows today's.

modifier_cumulative_tier.title: How does the price rise with use?
modifier_cumulative_tier.description: Some agreements charge more per kWh once your use passes a band. The bands are in your agreement. [How this works]({docs})

data_description.tiers: The use bands and their prices.
data_description.basis: Whether the bands count a month's use or a year's.

export.title: Do you sell electricity back?
export.description: If you export, what you are paid for it decides whether charging the battery beats selling. The amount follows on the next screen. [How this works]({docs})

data_description.mode: How your supplier pays for what you send out.

export_amounts.title: What do they pay you per kWh?
export_amounts.description: A negative export price is possible and PowerPlan does not hide it. [How this works]({docs})

data_description.amount: The fixed price, or what is subtracted from spot.
data_description.share: As a percent: 90 is 90 % of spot.

carriers.title: Do you also heat with gas, district heating, oil or pellets?
carriers.description: A heat pump competes with whatever else heats the home. Leave it empty if you only buy electricity. [How this works]({docs})

data_description.carriers: Each one asks for its price next.

carrier_gas.title: What does gas cost?
carrier_gas.description: The price per kWh of heat delivered, from your bill or agreement. [How this works]({docs})

data_description.mode: A number you type, or a sensor read once a day.
data_description.price: In your currency, per kWh of delivered energy.
data_description.entity_id: The sensor with today's price, if you chose a sensor.

carrier_district_heat.title: What does district heating cost?
carrier_district_heat.description: The price per kWh of heat delivered, from your bill or agreement. [How this works]({docs})

data_description.mode: A number you type, or a sensor read once a day.
data_description.price: In your currency, per kWh of delivered energy.
data_description.entity_id: The sensor with today's price, if you chose a sensor.

carrier_oil.title: What does heating oil cost?
carrier_oil.description: The price per kWh of heat delivered, from your bill or agreement. [How this works]({docs})

data_description.mode: A number you type, or a sensor read once a day.
data_description.price: In your currency, per kWh of delivered energy.
data_description.entity_id: The sensor with today's price, if you chose a sensor.

carrier_pellets.title: What do pellets cost?
carrier_pellets.description: The price per kWh of heat delivered, from your bill or agreement. [How this works]({docs})

data_description.mode: A number you type, or a sensor read once a day.
data_description.price: In your currency, per kWh of delivered energy.
data_description.entity_id: The sensor with today's price, if you chose a sensor.

tariff.title: Which grid company do you have?

data_description.country: Home Assistant has no country set, so it is asked here.
data_description.preset: Pick yours; if it is missing, pick Grid company not listed or Enter it myself.

tariff_preset.title: Does this match your grid bill?

data_description.confirm: No shows the grid companies again, with Enter it myself last.

tariff_target.title: Which capacity step do you want to stay in?
tariff_target.description: Automatic keeps you in the step you have already reached this month. [How this works]({docs})

data_description.target: Automatic, or a specific step with its monthly fee.
data_description.risk: Strict never goes above the target; the others may, within your {hours} highest hours.
data_description.target_kw: The kW to defend, for a tariff with no steps.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.description: Already filled in. Open it only if you know you want something else.

data_description.eps_kwh: Advanced: kWh of each window held back for meter delay and reaction time.
data_description.cap_margin_kw: Advanced: how far above the target the free ride may reach.

tariff_bills.title: What were your peaks the last twelve months?
tariff_bills.description: This tariff averages over a rolling year, so PowerPlan needs what you already used. Every field is optional; fill in what your invoices show. [How this works]({docs})

data_description.month_1: The highest measured value that month, in kW.
data_description.month_2: The highest measured value that month, in kW.

tariff_limits.title: How much power have you contracted?
tariff_limits.description: Your tariff contracts a power limit per period. The values shown are a common starting point; change them to what your own contract says. [How this works]({docs})

data_description.limit_1: The contracted power for this period.
data_description.limit_2: The contracted power for this period.
data_description.limit_3: The contracted power for this period.
data_description.limit_4: The contracted power for this period.

presence.title: Is anyone home?
presence.description: Comfort matters less in an empty house. PowerPlan can follow your Home Assistant people, or leave presence to you and your automations. [How this works]({docs})

data_description.mode: Automatic follows the people you pick next; otherwise an action or the presence entity decides.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.description: Already filled in. Open it only if you know you want something else.

data_description.away_delay_min: Advanced: time before an empty house counts as away.

presence_persons.title: Whose being away counts?
presence_persons.description: Everyone whose being away makes the house away. [How this works]({docs})

data_description.persons: Everyone whose being away makes the house away.

notifications.title: What should PowerPlan tell you?
notifications.description: Three things are worth an interruption; everything else is an entity you can put on a dashboard. A persistent notification always works, even before you have set up a notifier. [How this works]({docs})

data_description.peak_warning: This hour is heading over your capacity target.
data_description.comfort_violation: A room or a tank went below the floor you set.
data_description.notify_service: Which notify service the categories set to Send it to my phone use.
data_description.quiet_start: Nothing but the urgent gets through after this.
data_description.quiet_end: Normal notifications resume at this time.

data_description.peak_uncontrolled: The peak is coming from something PowerPlan does not steer.
data_description.deadline_at_risk: A charge or a cycle will not finish in time.
data_description.level_up: The month is about to move into a more expensive step.
data_description.price_source_dead: No prices have arrived for a day.
data_description.legionella_at_risk: A water heater's protection cycle cannot complete.
data_description.safe_mode: PowerPlan stopped steering and left every appliance as it was.
data_description.force_expired: A run now you started ran out and normal control resumed.

data_description.start_in_observe: Recommended: PowerPlan decides and explains but controls nothing, so you see what it would do first.

The export reading should be low unless you have solar panels.

[How this works]({docs})

data_description.confirm: Choose change to pick the sensors yourself.

postcode.title: What is your postcode?
postcode.description: Your postcode tells PowerPlan which taxes apply where you live. It is sent only to your country's official address register. [How this works]({docs})

data_description.postcode: Leave it empty to skip; you then pick your county if it matters.

tariff_product.title: Which grid tariff do you have with {operator}?
tariff_product.description: {operator} has more than one tariff for homes. It says which on your grid bill. [How this works]({docs})

tariff_zone.title: Which county do you live in?
tariff_zone.description: {operator} covers areas with different taxes, so PowerPlan needs to know where you live. [How this works]({docs})

tariff_confirm.title: Is this right for {operator}?

data.method: How your power step is worked out
data.inclusive: A peak exactly on a step's limit belongs to the step above
data.checked: These prices match my latest grid bill
data.no_power_fee: My bill has no power fee
data.measurement: How the demand charge is measured

modifier_supplier_tou.title: What does your supplier charge by time of day?
modifier_supplier_tou.description: Only your supplier's own day and night prices, if your contract has them. Your grid company's day and night charge is already included. [How this works]({docs})

data_description.periods: The periods and their prices per kWh.
data_description.fallback: Used for an hour no period covers.

state.title: Which support schemes apply to you?

data_description.schemes: Strømstøtte is paid automatically on your grid bill; it does not apply with Norgespris.
data_description.vat: PowerPlan has no VAT rate for your country: enter the one on your bill.

prices_format.title: How are these prices written?
prices_format.description: PowerPlan reads the sensor as {format}. Fill in what it could not tell from the sensor itself. [How this works]({docs})

data_description.attribute: The attribute that holds the list of prices.
data_description.tomorrow_attribute: Leave empty when tomorrow is in the same list.
data_description.start_key: The key in each row that holds when the price starts.
data_description.end_key: Leave empty when the rows have only a start.
data_description.value_key: The price's key; use dots for a nested one, such as price.amount.
data_description.currency: The three-letter code, for example NOK or EUR.
data_description.energy_unit: Whether a price is for one kWh or one MWh.
data_description.magnitude: Whole units, such as kroner and euros, or hundredths, such as øre and cents.
data_description.scale: 1 unless the prices are written in a fraction of a unit.
data_description.today_prefix: The part before the hour, for example price_ for price_07h.
data_description.tomorrow_prefix: Leave empty when the sensor has no hours for tomorrow.
data_description.home: The home to plan for, when your account has more than one.
data_description.incl_vat: Leave on unless you pay no VAT.
data_description.second_entity_id: The sensor with tomorrow's prices, usually found for you.

data_description.interval: Advanced: how long each price lasts.
data_description.granularity: Advanced: how long each price lasts.
data_description.slot_minutes: Advanced: how long each price lasts.

error.fuse_out_of_range: A main fuse is between 6 A and 400 A. Check the rating printed on the fuse.
error.phases_not_available: That phase count does not exist on this supply system.
error.power_unit_not_watts: A power sensor has to report watts or kilowatts.
error.energy_unit_not_kwh: An energy sensor has to report watt-hours, kilowatt-hours or megawatt-hours.
error.current_unit_not_amps: A current sensor has to report amps.
error.register_not_cumulative: This is not a running total. Pick the sensor that only ever goes up.
error.eps_looks_like_watts: This looks like watts. The guard band is energy: 0.30 kWh is the default for an hour-long window.
error.eps_not_positive: The guard band has to be more than zero.
error.target_above_fuse: This is above what the main fuse can ever deliver. Pick a lower step or target.
error.price_in_minor_unit: That is less than one øre or cent per kWh. The box is in øre (or cents), not kroner.
error.steps_too_few: Enter at least two steps from your bill.
error.steps_not_rising: Each step must go up to more than the one before it.
error.limit_required: Enter the power your contract gives you.
error.postcode_invalid: That does not look like a postcode here.
error.tariff_source_unreachable: Could not fetch the grid companies right now. Pick Grid company not listed or Enter it myself, or try again later.
error.price_format_unknown: PowerPlan does not recognize this sensor's prices. Choose the format that fits.

site_fixed_price_savings.name: Saved by the fixed price this month

unknown_site.message: Could not find the home {site}. Check that PowerPlan is set up and running.

unknown_load.message: No appliance with id {load} in this home.

set_peak_needs_a_day_or_a_month.message: Choose either a date or a month.

tariff_refresh_failed.message: Could not refresh the grid tariff from {source}: {reason}. The tariff PowerPlan has is kept.

engine_failing.title: PowerPlan is in fallback mode
engine_failing.description: PowerPlan failed {failures} times in a row ({error}) and has stopped steering; every appliance is left as it was. Restart Home Assistant; if this comes back, report it with the log.

battery_control_off.title: A battery is not steered
battery_control_off.description: PowerPlan cannot steer **{load}** through {integration}. Switch on {setting}, then reload the integration. Until then the battery runs on its own.

load_error.title: An appliance is on hold
load_error.description: {load} ran into an error ({error}) and is held as it is while the other appliances carry on. Check that the device answers in Home Assistant.

meter_stale.title: The grid meter stopped reporting
meter_stale.description: {site}: the power reading has not changed for more than ten minutes, so PowerPlan waits. Check that the meter's integration is running.

register_missing.title: No register report for a day
register_missing.description: {site}: the meter reading has not reported for 24 hours; PowerPlan counts from the power reading meanwhile. Check that the meter's integration is running.

scaling_mismatch.title: Power and register disagree
scaling_mismatch.description: {site}: the power reading and the meter reading have disagreed by more than 5 % for six hours. Check that both sensors use the right unit.

price_source_dead.title: Electricity prices are missing
price_source_dead.description: {site}: {source} has not delivered prices for 24 hours; PowerPlan estimates them meanwhile. Check that the price integration is running.

preset_outdated.title: The tariff preset has changed
preset_outdated.description: {site}: the grid tariff {preset} has changed since this home was set up, and the home keeps the one it has. To use the new one, choose Reconfigure on PowerPlan.

bound_helper_missing.title: A schedule, person or calendar is gone
bound_helper_missing.description: {site}: a schedule, person or calendar this home uses no longer exists. Choose Reconfigure and pick a new one.

role_missing.title: A required entity is gone
role_missing.description: {site}: an entity an appliance uses no longer exists. Open the appliance's setup and pick a new one.

provision_refused.title: A device refuses its provisioning
provision_refused.description: {site}: a device keeps refusing the settings PowerPlan needs. Check that the device is online and accepts changes.

legionella_at_risk.title: Legionella cycle at risk
legionella_at_risk.description: {site}: the water heater cannot finish its legionella heating in time. Check that the water heater is on and reachable.

delegated_idle.title: An appliance is not answering
delegated_idle.description: {site}: an appliance controlled by something else has not changed for 24 hours. Check the automation or integration that controls it.

savings_low_confidence.title: Savings figure is uncertain
savings_low_confidence.description: {site}: for a week, PowerPlan's estimate of what {load} would have used without it has missed, so its savings are uncertain. Nothing to do; it improves as PowerPlan learns.

notify_service_missing.title: Notification service missing
notify_service_missing.description: {site}: the notify service {service} does not exist, so notices appear in Home Assistant instead. Choose Reconfigure and pick another service.

store_reset.title: PowerPlan's saved data was reset
store_reset.description: {site}: PowerPlan could not read its saved data and moved it to {path}; this hour is rebuilt from the meter. Nothing to do; attach that file if you report it.

device_missing.title: An appliance's device is gone
device_missing.description: The appliance «{load}» no longer exists in Home Assistant. PowerPlan does not control it until you pick a new device: open PowerPlan, find «{load}» and choose Change setup.

prices_stale.title: Electricity prices are not up to date
prices_stale.description: {site}: PowerPlan has had no known prices since {since}. The plan uses estimated prices meanwhile, and PowerPlan retries automatically. If this lasts, check that the Nord Pool integration is loaded.

tariff_review.title: Confirm a tariff value you set
tariff_review.description: {site}: your own setting ({kept}) differs from what PowerPlan would use for your country or your grid company, so it is kept as yours. Select Submit to keep it; choose Reconfigure to change it.

tariff_stale.title: The grid tariff has run out
tariff_stale.description: {site}: the grid tariff from {operator} has no prices after its last period, and fetching new ones keeps failing. PowerPlan keeps using the last prices it has. Check your internet connection, or choose Reconfigure to pick the tariff again.

pv_forecast_unavailable.title: A PV forecast cannot be read
pv_forecast_unavailable.description: {site}: Home Assistant's energy forecast could not be read ({error}), so PowerPlan plans without a solar forecast. Check that your solar forecast integration is loaded.

options.user: which you chose here because Home Assistant has none set

options.weather_none: No weather forecast found in Home Assistant.
options.usage_meter: Normal usage is learned from the meter and offered after about two weeks.
options.usage_none: No meter, so no normal usage to learn.
options.fuse_assumed: The fuse size is assumed for your country.
options.first_setup: **What happens first** — {name} starts in trial mode: PowerPlan decides, explains and logs what it would have done, but controls no device until you turn automatic control on. Keep the box ticked for the first few days; they also calibrate the savings figures.
options.first_reconfigure: **What happens now** — whether PowerPlan controls your appliances stays as it is; change it with Automatic control on the home's device.

options.no_peak: No capacity charge: only the energy price matters.
options.metric_max_15: You pay for your highest quarter-hour {period}.
options.metric_max_30: You pay for your highest half-hour {period}.
options.metric_max_60: You pay for your highest hour {period}.
options.metric_top_n: You pay for the average of your {n} highest {windows}, {period}.
options.metric_top_n_days: You pay for the average of your {n} highest {windows} on {n} different days, {period}.
options.linear_month: The fee is {price} per kW per month.
options.linear_year: The fee is {price} per kW per year.
options.contracted_trip: Your connection is limited to {limits}; above that the supply trips.
options.contracted_surcharge: Your connection is limited to {limits}; above that costs extra.
options.assumed: Some numbers here are assumed, not verified: check them against your bill.
options.state_asked: PowerPlan has no tax rates for your country, so it uses the VAT you entered with your grid tariff.

options.unsure: We are not sure — check that this is the right appliance.

user.title: Which appliances should take turns?
user.description: Appliances that share power and take turns — six floor loops sharing 2 kW when the hour gets tight. PowerPlan serves the coldest first and rotates so none is left behind. [How this works]({docs})

data_description.name: What the group is called: the floor loops, the bedroom radiators.
data_description.members: The appliances that share power and take turns for it.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.description: When sharing starts, and how long an appliance waits before it goes first.

data_description.from_stage: The control level at which the group starts sharing.
data_description.ceiling_fraction: The hour's expected use, in percent of its target, at which the group shares anyway.
data_description.starve_seconds: How long an appliance may wait before it goes to the front of the queue.

review.title: Before this group is added
review.description:
**{name}** shares {max_concurrent_kw} kW between {members} when the hour gets tight: the coldest gets it first.

Sharing starts at control level {from_stage} or at {ceiling_fraction}% of this hour's target; an appliance that waits more than {starve_min} minutes goes first.

data_description.max_concurrent_kw: How much these appliances may draw at once, in total, while they share. Defaults to the two largest appliances' power summed.

user.title: Which heat sources share a room?
user.description: Appliances that heat the same room, such as a heat pump and a heated floor. PowerPlan runs whichever heats cheapest, and prefers the heat pump when the hour is tight. [How this works]({docs})

data_description.name: What the room is called: the living room, the bathroom.
data_description.members: The room's heating appliances; each brings its heat source and efficiency from its setup.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.description: The guards that stop a close call flapping between sources.

data_description.min_cop: Never engage a heat pump below this COP.
data_description.switch_hysteresis: How much cheaper, in percent, the other source must be before switching.
data_description.min_dwell_min: How long the running heater keeps the room before another may take over.
data_description.switch_confirm_s: How long a cheaper source must stay cheaper before the switch is taken.
data_description.capacity_penalty: Extra cost per kWh of electric heat while the hour's target is at risk.
